findings.claim: The learning window and observed score clocks span [0.0, 0.49] with 50 observed score nodes; curve support is [0.0, 0.49] and no extrapolation is permitted.
The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; coordinate contrasts are not themselves an affinity objective.

For landmark_00_local_dx the observed curve is non-monotone: it rises to a positive peak near the middle of the window, then falls to a negative trough, then partially recovers, with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches; the whole-window mean z is near zero (-0.18) and the quadratic fit is not accepted (relative node RMSE 0.78).

The first-node rate z is strongly negative (-17.5) while the last-node rate z is strongly positive (+8.1) for landmark_00_local_dx, indicating the local slope changes sign across the window rather than a stationary trend.

hypotheses.direction: test staged relevance (S1 observed-to-static) against the constant-blend control S2 at fixed dose; do not assume a monotone coordinate target
hypotheses.falsifier: if the staged schedule produces the same landmark_00_local_dx trajectory as the constant-blend control at matched dose, or if the sign reversal disappears under both, the stage-dependent relevance is not supported
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx predicted-endpoint world-coordinate contrast over observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: all seeds over the full observed support [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.statement: A stage-dependent teacher relevance schedule (early same-clock historical forecasts blending toward frozen static teachers) is worth testing at fixed dose for this coordinate, because the observed landmark_00_local_dx contrast is non-stationary with a sign reversal across the window rather than a constant offset.

hypotheses.direction: retain gradual/observed profile; reject a constant-direction coordinate objective
hypotheses.falsifier: if an independently stable profile shows a reproducible monotone trend with no strong sign conflicts, the non-monotone limitation would be overturned
hypotheses.observable: sign-change count and strong-sign-conflict count of the landmark_00_local_dx contrast
hypotheses.scope: all seeds over the full observed support
hypotheses.statement: Because the landmark_00_local_dx curve has 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches with a near-zero whole-window mean, a single global monotone coordinate target is not supported; any reward should be evaluated against the observed non-monotone profile rather than a fixed endpoint direction.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curves were read, so no data-derived stage knot is supported.
Only one coordinate feature (landmark_00_local_dx) was read in detail; other landmark coordinates were not inspected and may behave differently.
Selection preference and survival are not measured final affinity; no decoded final-affinity labels were available, so no claim about descendant survival or final benefit is made.
The observed contrast curve does not define an absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient; no such target is asserted.
